description: Independent ridge filter (multi-scale Hessian, dark lines, no geometry) on the 50 images of the multi-illumination aerial set: AUC of the filter reading on the pixels of each label layer against background rock, per image, per viewpoint and overall (median, minimum and maximum over the images in which the set has at least 30 pixels).
paper_items: supplement S4: an independent ridge filter, AUC table

units.auc: probability that the reading of a set pixel exceeds that of a background pixel (ties count one half)
units.d: image distance in pixels to the nearest pixel of the visible evidence

detector.luminance: 8-bit sRGB values of frame.png, Rec. 709 weights (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722)
detector.response: maximum over sigma of max(sigma^2 x larger Hessian eigenvalue, 0)
detector.reading: maximum of the response in the 3 x 3 neighbourhood

sets.U: unclear line on rock (u_line and region mask = 1)
sets.d: Euclidean distance to the nearest pixel of M = (opening_class > 0) or target or u_line
sets.B: background: valid pixels more than 20 px from M and from the occluded line, at most 200000 at a fixed stride

notes: The filter is set by hand; it is not a trained detector and does not stand for a human interpreter. It answers only whether a dark linear feature is present at the labelled position.
The reading is an absolute brightness curvature: in images partly in shadow it is affected by the division into lit and shadowed areas.

Background stride = ceil(candidates / 200000) in row-major order, see frames[*].background.step. O, O_near and O_far keep the pixels that coincide with the unclear line (n.O_and_U) and are not restricted to rock (n.O_off_rock).
